definitions.explanation: A series of objects or people arranged in a line.
A line of people waiting for something.

notes:
{列|れつ} refers to an arrangement of things or people in a line, row, or queue.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {行列|ぎょうれつ}: queue, procession, matrix (math)
- {列車|れっしゃ}: train
- {整列|せいれつ}: lining up, alignment
- {前列|ぜんれつ}: front row
- {後列|こうれつ}: back row
- {列島|れっとう}: archipelago, chain of islands

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {列|れつ}に{並|なら}ぶ: to stand in line
- {列|れつ}を{作|つく}る: to form a line
- {列|れつ}に{割|わ}り{込|こ}む: to cut in line
- {列|れつ}を{乱|みだ}す: to break ranks

USAGE:
{列|れつ} is more formal than {行列|ぎょうれつ} for queues. In daily speech, {並|なら}んでいる{人|ひと} (people lining up) is common.
